text: Risk management is the process of identifying, assessing, and controlling potential problems before they cause damage. The first step is identifying risks, which means looking carefully at what could go wrong in a project or business. Once risks are known, mitigation strategies can reduce their impact—for example, by improving safety procedures or diversifying suppliers. It is also wise to prepare contingency plans, which are backup plans used if a risk actually happens. Finally, monitoring is essential: risks change over time, so regular reviews help you spot new dangers and check whether your strategies still work. Good risk management does not remove all risk, but it helps you respond calmly and protect your goals.
